transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I'm mainly here because my sleep has just gotten completely unreliable lately. Like, I'll go to bed so exhausted—I'm a sales manager, and it's just been non-stop. Actually, my regional director just bought this massive boat, a catamaran I think, and he keeps sending the team pictures of it on our weekend group chat. Which honestly feels a little tone-deaf when we're all scrambling to hit our Q3 quotas, you know? He named it 'Out of Office,' if you can believe that. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right, my sleep. So even when I'm dead tired from all of that, I just lie there in bed replaying our sales forecasts and all these petty team issues. And then, if I finally do drift off, I almost always end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again. It just keeps spinning.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're lying awake at night replaying those sales forecasts and team issues?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's like... most days my mind just jumps from one thing to the next, like whether we'll actually hit the launch numbers, or if someone on my team is about to quit. Actually, speaking of my team, my assistant manager, Dave, he just got a new puppy. A golden doodle, I think? He keeps bringing it up on our zoom calls and holding it up to the camera, which is cute and all, but it completely derails the meeting. Like, we have an agenda, Dave! We only have thirty minutes to go over the pipeline! 

But, um, yeah, back to the worry thing. It's not just work, either. It jumps to the mortgage, or a client renewal, and it just feels like every small delay could turn into something major. It's exhausting.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm always worried, but it doesn't really peak like that. It's more like a constant hum in the background. Kind of like my refrigerator, actually. We just bought this new smart fridge—well, my husband bought it. He loves gadgets. It has a screen on the front where you can leave notes or see what's inside without opening the door. Which sounds great, but it syncs to our family calendar, and yesterday it reminded me about my dentist appointment while I was just trying to get some milk for my coffee. It was just sitting there, glaring at me. I hate the dentist. Dr. Miller is nice enough, but the scraping noise... ugh. But yeah, no sudden intense fear or anything like that. Just the regular, exhausting worry.
Do you feel tired or fatigued during the day, even after you've had some rest?

Yeah, I am always so tired. It's like I'm dragging myself through the day, honestly. Even on weekends, when I try to sleep in, I still wake up feeling like I ran a marathon. My husband keeps telling me I need to drink more water, which, I mean, he's probably right. He bought me one of those giant water bottles with the time markers on it, you know the ones? It says things like 'Keep going!' at 10 AM and 'Almost there!' at 4 PM. It's kind of aggressive for a water bottle, if you ask me. I left it at the office on Friday, actually, right next to the printer. Our printer has been jamming non-stop, by the way. It's driving the whole floor crazy. We put in a maintenance ticket three days ago, but IT is always so backed up. 

But um, wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being tired. Yeah, no matter what I do, I just feel completely drained all day long.
Do you find yourself feeling most alert or awake at the same time every day, regardless of when you go to bed or wake up?

Um... not really? I don't think there's a specific time I feel most awake. It's more like I'm just tired all the time, no matter what. Honestly, time just kind of blurs together lately. Speaking of time, though, did you know daylight saving time is coming up? I always dread it. The whole falling back thing just messes up my entire schedule. Plus, it gets dark at, like, 4:30 PM, which is just depressing. I was telling my sister about it on the phone yesterday—she lives in Arizona, so they don't even do daylight saving time. Which is so weird to me. Like, how do you just opt out of time? But she loves it there. She keeps telling me I should move out there, get some sun, maybe take up hiking. But I hate the heat, and honestly, the thought of packing up the house... ugh. We have so much junk in the garage. 

But, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about being alert. Yeah, no, I don't really have a time where I feel awake. I'm just always exhausted.
Do you have a regular bedtime and wake-up time every day?

I don't really know, honestly. I don't think I have a set schedule. I mean, I try to, but it's all over the place. Sometimes I'm in bed by 10, sometimes it's 1 AM because I get caught up checking emails. Being a sales manager means my inbox literally never stops. Last night I was looking at this one client's account, and I realized they're based in Seattle, which made me think about how much it rains there. Have you ever been to Seattle? My husband and I went a few years ago and we went to that big public market where they throw the fish. It's kind of gross if you really think about it, just raw fish flying through the air right over people's heads. And the smell... I had to buy a coffee just to hold it under my nose while we walked around. I've been trying to drink less coffee lately, actually, but decaf just tastes like sad brown water. 

But um... wait, sorry, what was the question? Something about my alarm clock?
Do you often find yourself feeling most tired or sluggish at the same time every day?

I don't think so? Like, I don't really hit a specific wall at, say, 2 PM or anything. It's just a constant, low-level exhaustion from the minute I wake up. Although, speaking of 2 PM, that's usually when the snack cart comes around at work. They have these little bags of pretzels that are so salty, but you can't stop eating them. I usually grab two. My coworker, Sarah, always gets the yogurt, which I don't understand because the fridge in the breakroom is definitely not keeping things cold enough. I told HR about it last week because someone's milk spoiled and the whole room smelled like old cheese. It was disgusting. We had to prop the door open with a trash can just to air it out. And then the cleaning crew came in and they used this lemon spray that just made it smell like lemon-scented rotten cheese. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Something about feeling sluggish? Yeah, no, I don't think it's a specific time. I'm just always tired.
Do you go to bed and wake up at different times on weekdays versus weekends?

Um, I don't really think so? It's kind of just a mess all week long, to be honest. Like, I don't really have a strict weekend routine either. Although, on Saturdays we usually try to go to the farmers market downtown, but finding parking is an absolute nightmare. Last weekend, someone actually dinged my car door while we were parked near the bakery stand. It's a relatively new car, too, so my husband was furious. He spent like an hour trying to pull the footage from the dashcam, but the memory card was full. Which is so typical, right? You buy these gadgets to protect yourself, and then when you actually need them, they don't even work. Kind of like my old printer in the home office. I spent half of Sunday trying to print out these quarterly reports for my sales team, and it just kept jamming. I swear, technology knows when you're stressed out. It makes this horrible grinding noise before it just completely eats the paper, and then you get ink all over your hands trying to pull it out. 

Wait, sorry... what were we talking about? Did you ask about my weekend plans?
Do you often go to bed at a significantly different time from one day to the next?

I mean, yeah, I guess so? It really just depends on the day and what's going on. Like I was saying about the emails, sometimes I'm up super late. And then other nights, I just crash on the couch while we're watching TV. We've been trying to watch that new true crime documentary series, but I can never make it through a whole episode without falling asleep. My husband gets so annoyed because he wants to talk about the clues, and I'm just out cold. But honestly, those shows are so creepy anyway. They always interview the neighbors, and the neighbors are always like, "He was such a quiet guy, kept to himself." Which makes you wonder, right? Like, the guy who lives next door to us, Mr. Henderson, he's super quiet. He's always out in his yard at like 6 AM trimming his rose bushes. And his roses are beautiful, don't get me wrong, but who is up that early just to garden? I tried to grow tomatoes last summer, and the squirrels ate every single one of them before they even turned red. I bought this special netting to put over the pots, but they just chewed right through it. They're basically tiny menaces with fluffy tails. 

Wait... what was the question? Something about going to bed? Yeah, I don't really have a set time. It's just whenever I finally stop moving.
Do you think your sleep problems started around the same time as the increased stress from your sales manager job?

I mean, yeah, I guess that makes sense. It's really been building up since they did that whole sales division reorganization, which was... gosh, about thirteen months ago now? That whole restructure was a complete nightmare. They brought in this consulting firm, right? And these guys in their expensive suits were just walking around with clipboards, looking at us like we were numbers on a spreadsheet. They ended up moving my desk from by the window to this interior cubicle that gets absolutely zero natural light. It's like a cave in there. I bought a little fake succulent to put on my desk just to have something green, because a real plant would definitely die. Speaking of dying plants, my sister tried to give me a peace lily for my birthday last month, and my cat, Barnaby, immediately started chewing on the leaves. I had to look it up online to see if it was toxic, and of course it is, so I had to put the plant up on top of the refrigerator where he can't reach it. But now I always forget to water it because it's out of sight, out of mind, you know? And Barnaby just sits on the counter staring up at it, plotting his next move. He's so stubborn. 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? The reorganization? Yeah, it's been about thirteen months of this building up.
Do you think your sleep problems are directly caused by the stress you're experiencing at work?

I mean, I don't really know if it's *directly* caused by work, you know? Like, work is definitely stressful, but is it the only thing keeping me awake? I'm not sure. Sometimes I think it's just my brain refusing to shut off. Like, the other night I was lying there, and I started thinking about whether I left the garage door open. Which is so stupid, because I haven't parked in the garage since we started using it for storage. We bought all these heavy-duty plastic bins to organize everything, but they're still just stacked up in the corner, totally empty. My husband keeps saying he's going to spend a weekend sorting through all his old college stuff, but he never does. He has this one box of old band t-shirts that he refuses to get rid of, even though they're completely full of holes. I tried to tell him we could turn them into a quilt or something, like I saw on Pinterest. I actually made a Pinterest board just for upcycling projects, but honestly, who has the time? You buy all the supplies, and then they just sit in a closet collecting dust, right next to the sewing machine I got for Christmas three years ago. I think I used it once to hem a pair of pants, and the thread kept bunching up underneath the fabric. It was so frustrating. 

Wait, what did you ask me? If work is causing the sleep stuff? I honestly don't know for sure. It's probably a mix of everything.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you had a more regular daily routine?

I mean, maybe? A routine sounds nice in theory, but I don't even know how I'd stick to one. Like, I tried to get into meal prepping a few months ago to be more organized. I bought all these matching glass containers with the snap-on lids, because the plastic ones always get stained if you put tomato sauce in them. Anyway, I spent a whole Sunday making this giant batch of quinoa and roasted vegetables, and by Wednesday, I was so sick of eating it that I ended up ordering Thai food instead. There's this place down the street from us that makes the best Pad See Ew. They always give you way too much food, though, so then you have leftovers taking up space in the fridge. Our fridge is already packed because my husband went on this huge hot sauce kick and ordered like twelve different bottles online. He has them all lined up on the top shelf, and half of them he hasn't even opened yet. I keep telling him we need to throw out the expired condiments, but he says hot sauce never really goes bad because of the vinegar. Which, I don't know, sounds fake to me. Vinegar has to expire eventually, right? Like, everything breaks down. 

Wait... what was the question? Something about a routine? Yeah, I don't know if that would fix the sleep thing. I'm just not great at sticking to schedules.
Do you have difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or both?

I mean, it's really both. Like, I'll go to bed completely exhausted, but I just lie there replaying all my sales forecasts and team issues in my head. And then, even if I do manage to fall asleep, I'll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and my brain just will not power down again. It's so frustrating because it's completely dark outside at that time. Sometimes I'll hear the garbage truck coming down the street, which is so loud. They always come on Tuesdays, except when there's a holiday, and then it shifts to Wednesday. Last week they forgot to take our recycling bin, which was completely full because we finally broke down all those cardboard boxes from when we bought the new patio furniture. The furniture is nice, it's this gray wicker stuff, but the cushions take forever to dry if it rains. I meant to buy a cover for it, but I went to Target and got totally distracted looking at the seasonal section. They already have Halloween stuff out, and it's not even October yet! I saw this little ceramic ghost holding a pumpkin that was really cute, but I didn't buy it because I have nowhere to put it. Our mantel is already crowded with framed photos that I've been meaning to hang on the wall for like, two years. 

Wait, sorry. What were you asking? Falling asleep or staying asleep? Yeah, it's definitely both. I just can't get my brain to stop.
Do you often go to bed and wake up at different times from day to day?

I mean, I don't really keep track of the exact times, so I'm not totally sure. It probably changes a lot depending on the day. Like, I always use my phone for my alarm, which everyone says is bad for your sleep hygiene or whatever, because then you just end up scrolling. Last night I was on Instagram and I fell down this huge rabbit hole watching videos of those dogs that use the talking buttons? You know, where they step on a button and a voice says "outside" or "treat"? My sister has a labradoodle and she actually bought a set of those. But her dog doesn't even try to talk, he just chews on them. She spent like fifty dollars on this starter kit, and now they're all covered in slobber and the speaker on the "play" button is completely busted. She's always buying ridiculous stuff for that dog, though. For his first birthday, she got him this organic, grain-free dog cake from a special pet bakery downtown. I didn't even know dog bakeries were a real thing until I went with her to pick it up. The whole store smelled like a mix of peanut butter and salmon, which was honestly kind of nauseating. And they had these little doggy mannequins in the window wearing yellow raincoats and matching boots. Who puts boots on a dog? 

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Something about my alarm clock? I don't really know when I go to sleep, honestly. It's just kind of all over the place.
Do you often go to bed at a time that is more than an hour different from the previous night?

I don't really know, honestly. I don't pay that much attention to the exact time on the clock. I just try to go to bed when I'm tired, but then I end up lying there forever anyway. I used to have this digital clock on my nightstand that projected the time onto the ceiling in red numbers. My husband bought it because he said he hated having to roll over to see what time it was. But it was so annoying! The red light was surprisingly bright, and it always felt like it was staring down at me, just reminding me how long I'd been awake. Plus, the projection was never quite straight, it was always tilted a little to the left, which drove me crazy. I tried adjusting the little dial on the side, but it was super sensitive, so if you bumped the table even a tiny bit, the numbers would move. We finally got rid of it when we painted the bedroom. We painted it this color called "Sea Salt," which is supposed to be really calming, but honestly, in certain lighting it just looks gray. I spent weeks looking at paint swatches at Home Depot. The guy at the paint counter probably thought I was insane. He kept trying to explain the difference between satin and eggshell finishes, but I just wanted a color that didn't look like a hospital waiting room. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Going to bed an hour different? I really have no idea. I just don't track it that closely.
Do you think your sleep schedule would be more regular if you weren't working as a sales manager?

I mean, maybe? But I'm not really sure. Work is definitely stressful, but I feel like even if I didn't have this job, I'd still find something else to stress about at night. Like, before I got promoted to manager, I was just a regular sales rep, and I still couldn't sleep. I used to cover the entire Midwest territory, which meant I was constantly flying out of O'Hare. O'Hare is the absolute worst airport to fly out of in the winter. One time, I got stuck there for fourteen hours because of a blizzard, and I had to sleep on the floor near my gate. I used my winter coat as a blanket, but it was one of those puffy down jackets that makes a weird swishing noise every time you move. And the floor was freezing. I tried to buy a coffee from Starbucks to warm up, but the line was literally wrapping around the terminal, and by the time I got to the front, they were completely out of oat milk. I can't drink regular milk anymore because it upsets my stomach, which is so annoying because I used to love eating cereal before bed. Honey Nut Cheerios were my favorite. I tried the almond milk version once, but it just tasted like sweet water. 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask if my sleep would be better if I wasn't a manager? I don't know, honestly. I think my brain is just wired to worry no matter what I'm doing.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you were to switch to a job with a more regular and predictable schedule?

I don't think a predictable schedule would really fix it, honestly. I mean, my schedule isn't even that crazy right now, it's just the pressure of the job. But even if I worked, like, a nine-to-five at a desk, I'd probably still be up worrying. My friend Sarah has a super predictable job—she works in HR for a dental supply company—and she still has terrible insomnia. She actually tried taking melatonin for it, but she said it gave her these insanely vivid nightmares. She told me about one where she was trapped in a giant hourglass and the sand was made of tiny little teeth. It sounded horrifying. She ended up throwing the whole bottle away. She's really into natural remedies now, though. She bought this essential oil diffuser that looks like a fake piece of wood, and she runs it all night with lavender and chamomile. I went over to her house last week and it smelled like a spa, but almost too strong, you know? Like, it kind of gave me a headache. She also has this weighted blanket that's supposed to help with anxiety, but it weighs like twenty pounds. I tried it once and it felt like I was being squashed by a heavy rug. I don't know how anyone sleeps under that. 

Wait, what was the question? A regular schedule? Yeah, I really don't think it would make a difference. My mind just doesn't know how to turn off.
Do you think your sleep would improve if you were not working as a sales manager?

I mean, I don't know if just quitting being a sales manager would magically fix things, because I'm here because my sleep has gotten so unreliable anyway. Like, even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there replaying all my sales forecasts and team issues. And then I'll finally fall asleep, but I'll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and I just can't get my brain to power down again. It's so frustrating. It reminds me of this one time my laptop got stuck in this weird reboot loop during a huge presentation. I was trying to show these quarterly projections to the VP of Sales, and the screen just kept flashing blue and then going black, over and over. I was sweating through my silk blouse, which was a nightmare because silk shows everything, and I had just bought it from this boutique downtown that has a strict no-return policy. The woman who owns the shop is so intimidating, she always wears these giant geometric necklaces and stares at you over her glasses. Anyway, the IT guy had to come up and literally pull the battery out of the laptop to get it to stop. I wish I could do that to my brain, just pull the battery out at 3 AM. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask? If not being a manager would help? Yeah, I don't know. The sleep thing is just so bad right now, I don't think changing jobs would just turn it off.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you were not working as a sales manager and had a less demanding work schedule?

I honestly don't think a less demanding schedule would fix it, because the sleep issues are just... they're always there, you know? Like, I'm sure it wouldn't hurt to have fewer emails, but my brain would just find a way to fill that space with other worries. Like, if I had a lighter schedule, I'd probably just start obsessing over my apartment. I've been meaning to reorganize my kitchen cabinets for months, but I just keep putting it off. I bought all these clear plastic bins from the Container Store because I saw this influencer on TikTok do it, and her pantry looked amazing. She even had custom labels printed for everything, like "Almonds" and "Quinoa." I tried to print labels using this cheap label maker I bought online, but the tape kept jamming, and then the ink smeared everywhere. It got all over my hands, and I had to use nail polish remover to get it off, which completely ruined my manicure. I had just gotten this really pretty pale pink gel polish, too. The salon I go to is right next to this amazing bakery, and I usually get a croissant after my appointment, but they were closed for renovations that day. 

Wait, what were we talking about? A less demanding schedule? Yeah, no, I don't think it would really matter. The anxiety just kind of follows me around no matter how much or how little I have on my plate.
Do you think your sleep would be better if you had a job with a standard Monday-to-Friday schedule?

I don't really think just having weekends off would change much. Like, a Monday-to-Friday thing sounds nice in theory, but my weekends are usually just as stressful because I'm trying to catch up on everything I didn't do during the week. Last weekend I actually tried to force myself to relax and went to this new outdoor farmer's market that opened up near the river. I went specifically to get this local raw honey because my sister swore it cured her seasonal allergies. She lives in Austin now, and the pollen there is supposed to be awful. She actually just adopted a golden retriever mix down there, and she sends me pictures of him sitting in fields of bluebonnets. He's so cute, but he chews up literally all her shoes. She had to buy this special bitter apple spray to put on her sneakers just to get him to stop. Anyway, the honey guy at the market wasn't even there, so I ended up buying this twelve-dollar loaf of artisanal sourdough bread instead. It had kalamata olives baked into it, which was a huge mistake because I actually hate olives. I spent like twenty minutes picking them all out with a fork before I could even make a piece of toast. And the crust was so hard it actually scratched the roof of my mouth, you know when that happens? It's the absolute worst, it hurts for days every time you eat anything salty. 

Wait, sorry, what did you just ask me? Something about working Monday to Friday? Yeah, no, I just don't think the days of the week matter to my brain. It's going to keep me up regardless of what day it is.
